cards.explanation: The answer is some elders and leaders of the priests. The LORD says, "Take some of the elders of the people and leaders of the priests…" (Jeremiah 19:1). Those are the ones named to go along. Jeremiah gets a jar and some company for the road trip, friends.

The answer is Judah. Jeremiah is told to say, "Hear the word of the LORD, O kings of Judah and residents of Jerusalem." (Jeremiah 19:3). Judah is the kingdom, and Jerusalem is its city. This message has a very clear address on the envelope, bakers.

The answer is that they abandoned Him for other gods. The LORD says, "…they have abandoned Me and made this a foreign place. They have burned incense in this place to other gods…" (Jeremiah 19:4). The text names the cause right there, friends. No guessing needed.

The answer is False. The LORD says they burned incense to other gods "…that neither they nor their fathers nor the kings of Judah have ever known." (Jeremiah 19:4). So their fathers and the kings did not know these gods. Those are the gods the incense went to.

The answer is True, and the LORD is very clear about it. He says it was "…something I never commanded or mentioned, nor did it even enter My mind." (Jeremiah 19:5). That is as plain as words get, friends. He didn't ask for it, and He didn't even think of it.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "…I will give their carcasses as food to the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth." (Jeremiah 19:7). It's a hard picture, and I think it's meant to be. This verse is part of the weight of the warning.

The answer is that they will be appalled and scoff at her wounds. The LORD says, "All who pass by will be appalled and will scoff at all her wounds." (Jeremiah 19:8). The people passing by react with shock and scoffing. I think this part stings, friends, because the city ends up an object of scorn.

The answer is that it can never again be repaired. The LORD says, "I will shatter this nation and this city, like one shatters a potter’s jar that can never again be repaired." (Jeremiah 19:11). That's why the jar gets smashed in front of the men. They see for themselves what a broken jar looks like. Nobody's gluing that one back together, bakers.

The answer is Topheth. The LORD says, "They will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no more room to bury them." (Jeremiah 19:11). It's the same spot in the Valley of Ben-hinnom where Jeremiah was sent. A heavy detail, friends, so we'll let it sit.

The answer is that they poured out drink offerings to other gods. The LORD says the houses were those "…on whose rooftops they burned incense to all the host of heaven and poured out drink offerings to other gods." (Jeremiah 19:13). So the rooftops held both the incense and the drink offerings. Both were offered to gods other than the LORD.

The answer is the courtyard of the house of the LORD. The text says, "…he stood in the courtyard of the house of the LORD and proclaimed to all the people…" (Jeremiah 19:14). Jeremiah went from the valley to a place where people gather, friends. Now the whole crowd gets the message.

The answer is True. Jeremiah proclaims what the LORD of Hosts says: "…I am about to bring on this city and on all the villages around it every disaster I have pronounced against them…" (Jeremiah 19:15). So it isn't only Jerusalem, bakers, because the villages around it are named too. The announcement names the city and its villages together.
